result.summary: This pull request moves ownership of optional indexes (`g_txindex`, `g_txospenderindex`, `g_coin_stats_index`, and `g_filter_indexes`) from process-global singletons into `NodeContext`. It extracts block filter index management into `node/indexes.{h,cpp}` and passes index lookup into `PeerManager` via an options callback. RPC, REST, and test callers are updated to reference indexes through `NodeContext` instead of global pointers.
result.problem: Process-global index variables obscure object lifecycles during init and shutdown and hinder running multiple node instances or separating processes. Node subsystems and RPC handlers were directly accessing global index pointers.

resolved_concerns: Sjors asked how this PR interacts with #24230; w0xlt clarified that #24230 modifies sync logic and decoupling from node internals while keeping global ownership, making this ownership refactor orthogonal.

result.card: This PR moves ownership of optional indexes (txindex, txospenderindex, coinstatsindex, and block filter indexes) from process-global variables into NodeContext, registering index lifecycle explicitly during node startup and shutdown. It decouples the block filter index registry into node/indexes.{h,cpp} and adapts RPC and net_processing call sites to access indexes through NodeContext. The change is an internal refactoring that supports multiprocess goals and cleaner test isolation without modifying user-visible behavior. The PR has Concept ACKs from sedited and fjahr and is ready for detailed code review.
